# Tic-Tac-Toe: Proposed Canon Draft r3

Status: in-progress; readiness: not-assessed. Owner: ADHOC-7fd789738d5348cbbbd4f4cb378fbecf, workflow.planning. This current reconciliation supersedes tic-tac-toe-canon-r2 as the draft head, preserving r2 and r1 as its exact predecessors. It is not a complete proposal, admitted Canon or implementation approval. Retained candidates below keep their existing meaning and revision; additions/revisions are explicit.

## Inputs And Coverage

Input capture SHA-256: 8289cd57bc65e6500343a094190e10c8ab7c1ad6ff95eca307b8bd3262d6e788. Prior Canon request pins: r1 7ac28f9bf3aca134f6f52fb082868610db59a3bb17bdbe3b4e90603522e430c4; r2 9b92df3a13224d02f539ad22626a6ea70a976252dbaf25d307c1431f5c4da21e. All five source documents were inventoried and reconciled; none was omitted or only counted.
- source-1 d6139844ec225d1e36ddd07d9552bc8aa1a64fc14a38fc6b935560f49bea69ed: original game, modes, AI and mark choice.
- source-2 7af814bf2cd85e7440edec3184c9e505435e77ebf8d7fad2359c3b2ed884e961: manual replay.
- source-3 3546cbb855ed4253554279579fe77387fb3eaccfe03310fe79b5f2db2e44e616: Express/3630 and desktop/mobile.
- source-4 677069c28c0a4c38ba1772b07b82c664fd8c82a29f1465615b8488424e9f90b8: shared-device/no-persistence scope, all-mode replay, 500 ms pacing and actual phone testing.
- source-5 46d3113d1fd032c0a194c49229f11a956bf1b2de43b49f01e38df51d40417726: browser-held state, Start/setup behavior, Chrome on desktop/iPhone and this repository as destination.

The Operator's latest decisions resolve earlier recommendations only where stated. The checklist sample, PokerNight inception pack, old horizons and unrelated framework work remain outside the source corpus; choosing this repository does not import their requirements into this feature.

## Retained Candidate Set

Retain definitions d-human-count@r1, d-ai@r1, d-game@r1 and d-replay@r1 from r1. Their owner remains this capture's proposed product vocabulary, with original aliases, distinctions and source pins; none changes installed governance vocabulary.

Retain requirements r-rules@r1, r-modes@r2, r-mark-choice@r1, r-unbeatable@r1, r-result@r1, r-manual-replay@r2, r-react@r1, r-runtime@r1, r-local-session@r1 and r-ai-pacing@r1 exactly as defined in r1/r2. In particular retain exhaustive AI verification as either mark, X-first standard rules, 500 ms AI delay, all-mode human-triggered replay with mode/mark retention, fixed local port 3630, and no accounts/saved games/persistent scores. Their existing acceptance cases remain applicable. Replace only r-browsers@r2 as described next.

## Changed Candidates

- r-browsers@r3 (requirement; revise r-browsers@r2; sources 3-5): required browser acceptance targets are Chrome on desktop and Chrome on a physical iPhone accessing the local Express server over Wi-Fi. Preserve all responsive-layout, pointer/touch, full-game, replay and result-visibility criteria from r2. Test the named browser on the actual phone; desktop Chrome viewport emulation or a different mobile browser cannot substitute. Record the actual desktop OS, iPhone model/iOS version, Chrome versions, viewport and local access URL at verification. The earlier wider Safari/Firefox/Android matrix was a recommendation and is not a release gate for this scope. Additional engine testing is optional supplemental evidence. Uses r-runtime@r1, r-modes@r2 and r-start-setup@r1.

- r-state-authority@r1 (requirement; add; source-5): the browser owns transient game state and applies rule, controller, AI, turn and terminal-result transitions; Express serves the React application. No server gameplay API or shared cross-device game state is required by this agreed design. Acceptance: gameplay does not require server move-validation or opponent endpoints; independent browser sessions do not share a board. Verify the implementation follows the no-saved-game/persistent-score scope while retaining current settings for replay. This is not an offline-loading guarantee: the server must serve the app, and cached/offline delivery is not required. Uses r-react@r1, r-runtime@r1 and r-local-session@r1. Algorithm/library, component structure and internal APIs remain implementation choices.

- r-start-setup@r1 (requirement; add; source-5): initial setup allows mode selection and, in one-human mode, human X/O choice. A Start button begins the game with X first; no human or AI move occurs before Start. Mode and mark changes are disabled while the game is active and become available after termination. Play again retains current selections and begins another game as already specified, without another Start confirmation. Acceptance: exercise Start in all three modes, human O opening via AI after 500 ms, disabled setup controls throughout active play, and re-enabled controls at terminal state. A completed board/result remains visible until an explicit new-game action. Merely editing terminal setup selections does not schedule moves; starting uses the displayed selections. These last interaction details are acceptance elaboration of the agreed Start/manual-replay flow, not a new feature. Uses r-rules@r1, r-modes@r2, r-mark-choice@r1, r-manual-replay@r2 and r-ai-pacing@r1.

## Story Reconciliation

Retain the four story identities and revise them to r3 only to integrate the settled setup/state/browser constraints; no story is removed.
- s-solo@r3: choose X/O, press Start and play an unbeatable AI, then replay with the same selections. Trace: r-rules@r1, r-modes@r2, r-mark-choice@r1, r-unbeatable@r1, r-result@r1, r-manual-replay@r2, r-ai-pacing@r1, r-start-setup@r1 and r-state-authority@r1.
- s-watch@r3: press Start to observe two unbeatable AIs with 500 ms turn pacing, retain the draw, and decide when to Play again. Trace: r-modes@r2, r-unbeatable@r1, r-result@r1, r-manual-replay@r2, r-ai-pacing@r1 and r-start-setup@r1.
- s-two-humans@r3: two people choose the shared-device mode, start, alternate legal moves, see the result and choose replay. Trace: r-rules@r1, r-modes@r2, r-result@r1, r-manual-replay@r2, r-local-session@r1 and r-start-setup@r1.
- s-local-browser@r3: use Chrome on desktop or a physical iPhone over local Wi-Fi to play the browser-held React game served by local Express on 3630. Trace: r-react@r1, r-runtime@r1, r-browsers@r3, r-local-session@r1 and r-state-authority@r1.

## Resolved Questions And Remaining Preconditions

Resolved: setup-change policy and initial Start; browser state ownership/Express serving; required browser families and physical-device class; this repository as the intended destination. Earlier suggestions to isolate this feature in another repository or treat PokerNight product scope as a blocker are superseded by source-5. Do not ask those same questions again absent a concrete conflict. Exact device/browser versions are evidence to record, not a reason to invent or request advance version numbers now.

The chosen repository is /Users/jmsimpson/Documents/GitHub/PokerNight. The target branch and exact operational specification/execution baseline are not chosen by 'land it in this repo'. No baseline is initialized and no Git effect is authorized by these draft operations. Complete proposal/admission still needs that explicit base, full work contract and current review/decision. Product source location and compatible dependency/toolchain versions are implementation-context choices to reconcile against this repository, not new product requirements.

## Impact And Preservation

The resulting candidate set contains four unchanged definitions, thirteen requirements (ten retained, one revised, two added) and four revised stories. All keys are local candidates, not admitted identities. Source bytes and old drafts remain immutable. There is no inherited independent review or approval. Work r1's design/browser/destination questions now have answers; the separately authorized work reconciliation must consume this exact r3 and refresh its traces and acceptance guidance. This Canon operation does not itself rewrite work r1.

State-authority and Start constraints add implementation/testing obligations: prove browser state separation, pre-Start inactivity and active-game setup lock, and cancel stale AI actions. Actual Chrome-on-iPhone evidence is needed; emulation alone cannot satisfy it. LAN serving must be deliberate and must not imply public hosting or firewall changes during planning. Existing AI/timer/mobile/port risks and their mitigations in r1/r2 remain.

No existing implementation/completed-phase compliance was assessed and no phase is reopened. No tracker, phase prompt, repository DAG edge or execution state is changed. Relationship endpoints above refer to retained or newly declared candidate revisions. Only definition/requirement/story kinds are used; rich provenance and acceptance relationships remain textual, with no schema expansion. Current terminal condition remains in-progress, readiness not-assessed.
questions: Select the target branch and exact operational specification/execution baseline before a complete proposal or admission; the repository destination itself is settled.
